rounds.fact: Tripod was a major free website-builder alongside GeoCities and Angelfire, and was eventually bought by Lycos as part of its portal strategy in the late 90s.
Break.com built its early audience around viral videos aimed specifically at young men, a more niche focus than general-purpose video sites like YouTube.
RealPlayer's streaming format was, for years, the primary way people watched video and listened to audio online, long before YouTube or Spotify existed.
eBaum's World built its early traffic on hosting viral videos and flash animations, and was frequently accused of re-uploading other creators' content without credit.
LAUNCH (later LAUNCHcast) was one of Yahoo's earliest music properties, offering personalized internet radio years before Pandora or Spotify existed.
